concept.name: Volatility expansion
concept.definition: A measurable increase in price volatility — widening bar ranges, rising standard deviation, expanding volatility bands — typically accompanying breakouts and trend legs. It is the mirror of volatility contraction and marks regimes where price travels further per unit time.
concept.intuition: The quiet market wakes up: bars get longer and price starts covering ground fast.
concept.mechanics: Quantified by rising Bollinger BandWidth (bands widen automatically as the standard deviation of price increases), rising ATR, or rising historical volatility; observed visually as a sequence of wide-range directional bars.
concept.failure_modes: Volatility expansion cuts both ways: it raises opportunity and risk simultaneously, and late entries during expansion phases suffer the widest adverse excursions.
concept.misconceptions: That expanding volatility is bullish; it is direction-neutral — crashes are volatility expansions too.
concept.example: A stock breaking out of a months-long base prints daily ranges three times its recent average, and its Bollinger Bands widen sharply as the new trend leg begins.
